proof:
Source: step 7(b)–(e) of the parent proof, with an abstract Q in place of P̂. The hypotheses are exactly the facts used there: ‖P̂(v)‖ ≤ 1, P̂(v) fixes range Dψ(v), ‖DP̂(v)‖ ≤ a, |w| ≤ b|Dψ(v)w|, and β|ν| ≤ 1/2 with β = ab. (The parent then applies |ν| ≤ |x − y|.) Write v := g(x), ν := x − ψ(v), A := Dg(x), B := Dψ(v) and π := ψ∘g. By the chain rule, Dπ(x) = B∘A.
1. Let F(z) := Q(g(z))(z − ψ(g(z))).
- z ↦ Q(g(z)) is differentiable at x with derivative h ↦ DQ(v)(Ah) (chain rule).
- z ↦ z − ψ(g(z)) is differentiable at x with derivative h ↦ h − BAh.
By the product rule for applying an operator-valued map to a vector-valued map (Mathlib HasFDerivAt.clm_apply), F is differentiable at x with DF(x)h = Q(v)(h − BAh) + (DQ(v)(Ah))ν.
2. F vanishes on the open neighbourhood O of x, so F has derivative 0 at x. By uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative, DF(x) = 0. Hence Q(v)h − Q(v)(BAh) + (DQ(v)(Ah))ν = 0 for every h ∈ ℝ^P.
3. By the hypothesis Q(v)∘B = B, Q(v)(BAh) = BAh = Dπ(x)h. Therefore Dπ(x)h = Q(v)h + (DQ(v)(Ah))ν.
4. Estimate. |Q(v)h| ≤ ‖Q(v)‖|h| ≤ |h|, and |(DQ(v)(Ah))ν| ≤ ‖DQ(v)(Ah)‖|ν| ≤ ‖DQ(v)‖|Ah||ν| ≤ a|Ah||ν|. The hypothesis with w := Ah gives |Ah| ≤ b|BAh| = b|Dπ(x)h|. Put s := ab|ν|; then 0 ≤ s ≤ 1/2, using a, b ≥ 0. So |Dπ(x)h| ≤ |h| + s|Dπ(x)h|.
5. Hence (1 − s)|Dπ(x)h| ≤ |h|. Since 0 ≤ s ≤ 1/2, (1 + 2s)(1 − s) = 1 + s(1 − 2s) ≥ 1. So |Dπ(x)h| ≤ (1 + 2s)(1 − s)|Dπ(x)h| ≤ (1 + 2s)|h|.
6. As h is arbitrary and 1 + 2s ≥ 0, ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1 + 2s = 1 + 2ab|ν| (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound). ∎
key_steps: Differentiate F(z) = Q(g(z))(z − ψ(g(z))), which vanishes on O, at x: Q(v)(h − Dπ(x)h) + (DQ(v)(Dg(x)h))ν = 0.
Q(v) fixes Dπ(x)h = Dψ(v)Dg(x)h, so Dπ(x)h = Q(v)h + (DQ(v)(Dg(x)h))ν.
With s = ab|ν| ≤ 1/2, (1 − s)|Dπ(x)h| ≤ |h| and (1 + 2s)(1 − s) ≥ 1 give ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1 + 2s.
